newsitem.title: USA: CME Sep lumber ends limit up, Sep, Nov set highs.
newsitem.headline: CME Sep lumber ends limit up, Sep, Nov set highs.

text.p: September CME lumber futures closed up the daily $10 per tbf limit and posted a contract high as well as the highest price in 2-1/2 years on talk of Hurricane Edouard and strong cash lumber prices, traders said.
September ended limit up at $410.90 per tbf, which was also a new high while November set a high of $372.00 before ending at $371.40, up $8.90. Other months ended $2.90 higher to $1.10 lower.
"It (hurricane) gave shorts one more reason to cover," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst, citing short covering that developed during the day.
Weather forecasts said Edouard, a Category 3 hurricane, could hit Florida or the U.S. East Coast in five or six days.

Cash markets were especially strong for prompt wood and there could be added fill-in business on concern that the hurricane may hit the United States and spur demand for lumber for repair work in the aftermath of any possible damage, cash sources said.

Futures had started easier on profit taking before drifiting up on support from the firm cash market. Hurricane concerns added to strength after midsession and prices ran up sharply by midday, traders said.
